title: Tatsuki Fujimoto Before Chainsaw Man: 22-26
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: An anthology of four early one-shots by the creator of Chainsaw Man: a boy who plays underwater piano for a mermaid, a boy who wakes up as a girl and must rethink his relationships, a brother caring for a horned sister prophesied to end the world, and a girl humiliated when her sister's prize-winning nude portrait of her is put on display.
life_message: It holds up facing hard truths about oneself and the people one loves, even when the world sees them as monsters.

content.note: Nayuta is blamed for deaths and feared as an apocalypse bringer (Wikipedia); critics note Fujimoto's 'overwhelming violence' (Real Sound, cited in Wikipedia); MU Blood and Gore.

Dignity vs honor.evidence: Mitsuko vows to make her sister suffer for her humiliation (Wikipedia 'Sisters').

Order vs freedom.evidence: Characters break with expectations: Toshihide redefines his identity (Wikipedia).

Civic vs kin.evidence: Siblings carry two of four stories: Kenji and Nayuta, Mitsuko and Kyoko (Wikipedia).

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: Art-school prize traditions and peer pressure, little rank deference (Wikipedia).

Tradition vs secular-rational.evidence: Prophecy and mermaid myth used as fable in a secular world (Wikipedia).

Survival vs self-expression.evidence: Art, music and identity are central (Wikipedia; AniList Drawing).

folkways.japan: Art-school traditions of displaying prize work, schoolroom harassment and folk legends of mermaids and prophecy reflect Japanese school and folklore settings.

delivery.evidence: No review consulted on delivery; summaries show the message carried by plot and character choices (to verify).
delivery.note: The sources say little about delivery, so the default reading is that the message rides on the story's events.

winners_losers: Sympathy goes to outsiders: the mermaid's son, the transformed boy, the feared Nayuta and the humiliated sister; crowds that ostracize them are shown as cruel.
